mainText:
If you only remember one thing: A I is getting more capable and more dangerous at the same time, and regulators are moving from principles to incident response.

Number one. From your Rundown. Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark told the I M F and World Bank annual meetings that the singularity has now begun. He pointed to scores on Humanity's Last Exam rising from eight percent to nearly sixty eight percent since last year. Another benchmark, FrontierMath, went from two percent to ninety four percent. One Anthropic model projects a forty four trillion dollar U S economy by twenty thirty if A I spreads fast, with very disruptive job impacts. He says there are only a small number of years to act. Why it matters: a builder is saying this out loud to the people who run the global economy.

Number two. Also from your Rundown. Security firm NorForge says a hacker let A I agents do nearly all the work of breaking into over one hundred company websites. Victims include Cummins, Deere, and SharkNinja. The estimated cost was about fifty dollars per break in. The agents ran on open source tools left online with no password. Why it matters: offensive A I is getting cheap faster than defense is.

Number three. From your E U A I Act Newsletter. The European Commission held a special meeting on recent A I loss of control incidents. It has questioned more than thirty companies, including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta, about safety and copyright compliance. It also issued guidance on working with outside evaluators. Hungary wants E U safety teams embedded inside frontier labs. And the first harmonised A I Act standard has now been published. Why it matters: oversight is shifting from principles to incident response.

Number four. From your That One A I newsletter. The Department of Homeland Security banned DeepSeek from federal civilian agencies. The same weekend, DeepSeek shipped a faster version of its Flash model. Why it matters: for government and regulated buyers, your model list is now part of the deal.

Quick hits. OpenAI's GPT Live one point one brings new ChatGPT voices in French, German, Hindi, Mexican Spanish, Korean and Japanese. The A P I comes next. Perplexity's Computer can now rebuild apps by studying how they behave, with no source code. Inception's Mercury three claims speed gains over rivals. And WIRED asks why the people building A I think it could kill us all.

Good news. External testing is becoming normal. The E U is formally encouraging independent evaluators, like METR, to check powerful models before problems spread.

Also in your Reads: The New Yorker has Adam Gopnik on the protests in France.

The thread today: capability is racing ahead, and the guardrails are finally catching up. That's your briefing.
